topics.title: Smaller units and tenths as fractions

learn.hook: Your eraser is 'about 4 cm'? Not good enough for a scientist — let's measure between the marks!
points: Measuring in whole cm is not precise: a bead may lie between the 1 cm and 2 cm marks.
Divide each cm into 10 equal parts. Each part is 1/10 cm (one tenth, which is 1 mm).
The scale with the smallest equal marks gives the most accurate measurement.
4 cm and 6 tenths is the mixed number 4 6/10 cm, which is the improper fraction 46/10 cm.
We read 4 6/10 as 'four and six tenths'.

example.q: A crayon reaches 4 full cm and 6 small parts more, where each cm has 10 equal parts. Write its length in three ways.
steps: Words: four and six tenths cm

learn.reallife: A tailor's tape and your school scale both have tiny marks between the cm marks so that clothes and drawings fit exactly.

games.title: Tenth truths
items: A scale with only cm marks gives the most precise length of an ant
An ant is shorter than 1 cm; we need smaller marks.
Each tenth of a cm is 1 mm
1 cm = 10 mm, so one tenth of a cm is 1 mm.
A scale with 10 parts per cm is more accurate than one with 2 parts per cm
Smaller parts let us measure more exactly.

quiz.q: Why is a scale with only cm marks not enough to measure an eraser exactly?
options: cm is too big for every object
Its length may fall between two cm marks
quiz.explain: The eraser's end may land between two cm marks, so we need smaller parts.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every object is a whole number of units long

quiz.q: Each cm on a scale has 10 equal parts. A pin covers 3 cm and 7 parts. How long is it?
quiz.explain: Each part is 1/10 cm, so 7 parts = 7/10 cm. Length = 3 7/10 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each small part is a hundredth

quiz.q: Write 2 7/10 as an improper fraction.
quiz.explain: 2 wholes = 20 tenths. 20 + 7 = 27 tenths = 27/10.
quiz.mistake: Adds the whole and the numerator: 2 + 7 = 9

quiz.q: Write 43/10 as a mixed number.
quiz.explain: 43 tenths = 40 tenths + 3 tenths = 4 wholes and 3 tenths.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the whole part and the tenths

quiz.q: How do we read 5 3/10?
quiz.explain: 5 is the whole part and 3/10 is three tenths.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up tenths and hundredths

quiz.q: Which scale gives the most accurate measurement?
options: Each cm divided into 2 equal parts
Each cm divided into 10 equal parts
quiz.explain: The smaller the equal parts, the more exactly we can read a length.
quiz.mistake: Thinks bigger marks are easier and so more accurate

quiz.q: How many tenths are there in 6 1/10?
quiz.explain: 6 wholes = 60 tenths, plus 1 tenth = 61 tenths.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 and 1 instead

quiz.q: Write 'seven and nine tenths' as an improper fraction.
quiz.explain: 7 wholes = 70 tenths; 70 + 9 = 79 tenths = 79/10.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits in the wrong order

teach.ask: Gappu measured a leaf as '6 cm' but it is a bit longer. How can Gappu measure it better and write the length?
teach.praise: Perfect! Gappu measures leaves like a botanist now.
teach.nudge: Into how many equal parts can Gappu split each cm?

learn.hook: What is smaller than 1 but bigger than 0? A whole secret world of numbers lives behind the decimal point!
points: Cut one whole into 10 equal parts. Each part is one tenth, written 1/10 or 0.1.
Cut one whole into 100 equal parts. Each part is one hundredth, written 1/100 or 0.01.
The decimal point separates the whole part (on the left) from the parts smaller than one (on the right).
2.7 means 2 wholes and 7 tenths, that is 2 + 7/10.
10 tenths make 1 whole, and 10 hundredths make 1 tenth.

steps: The whole part is 3, so write 3 before the point
4 tenths go in the first place after the point
6 hundredths go in the second place after the point

learn.reallife: A fever of 100.2 °F, a long jump of 3.45 m and prices like ₹49.50 all use decimals.

quiz.q: Which decimal shows 7/10?
quiz.explain: 7/10 means 7 tenths. The first place after the point is tenths, so it is 0.7.
quiz.mistake: Puts the 7 in the hundredths place

quiz.q: Meena ate 3 of the 10 equal pieces of a chocolate bar. What decimal part of the bar did she eat?
quiz.explain: 3 pieces out of 10 equal pieces is 3/10 = 0.3.
quiz.mistake: Writes the part she did not eat, or puts 3 in the hundredths place

quiz.q: Write 2 + 5/10 + 8/100 as a decimal.
quiz.explain: 2 is the whole part, 5 goes in the tenths place and 8 in the hundredths place: 2.58.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the tenths and hundredths places

quiz.q: How many hundredths are there in 0.4?
quiz.explain: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 4 tenths = 40 hundredths. Indeed 0.4 = 0.40.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 4 tenths is the same as 4 hundredths

quiz.q: Which fraction is the same as 0.09?
quiz.explain: 0.09 has 9 in the hundredths place, so it is 9 hundredths = 9/100.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one digit after the point always means tenths

quiz.q: What is 15 tenths written as a decimal?
quiz.explain: 10 tenths make 1 whole. 15 tenths = 10 tenths + 5 tenths = 1.5.
quiz.mistake: Writes the 15 straight after the point

quiz.q: Arjun's school is 1 km and 3 tenths of a km from his home. Which decimal shows this?
quiz.explain: 1 whole km and 3 tenths is 1 + 0.3 = 1.3 km.
quiz.mistake: Puts the 3 in the hundredths place

quiz.q: What does 0.25 mean?
quiz.explain: In 0.25 the 2 is in the tenths place and the 5 is in the hundredths place.
quiz.mistake: Reads the digits after the point in the wrong places

teach.ask: Gappu sees 0.3 written on a juice bottle label. What does 0.3 mean? Explain it to him!
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! 3 out of 10 equal parts — Gappu understands now!
teach.nudge: Into how many equal parts do we cut the whole for tenths?

topics.title: Adding, subtracting and ordering tenths and hundredths

learn.hook: 13 tenths is too many to sit in the tenths place — 10 of them jump up and become 1 whole!
points: Add tenths like ones: 2 6/10 + 1 7/10 = 3 13/10 = 4 3/10 (10 tenths regroup as 1 whole).
Subtract with borrowing: 5 2/10 − 2 6/10 → borrow 1 whole as 10 tenths: 4 12/10 − 2 6/10 = 2 6/10.
To order lengths, compare the wholes first, then the tenths.
A length of 3 m, 4 tenths and 5 hundredths of a metre is 3 45/100 m.
100 hundredths make 1 whole, and 10 hundredths make 1 tenth.
learn.reallife: When you add two pieces of cloth or ribbon, the tailor adds metres and parts of a metre exactly like this.

quiz.explain: Wholes: 3. Tenths: 6 + 7 = 13 tenths = 1 whole and 3 tenths. Total 4 3/10.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to regroup 10 tenths as 1 whole

quiz.explain: 2 tenths is less than 6 tenths, so borrow: 4 12/10 − 2 6/10 = 2 6/10.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the smaller tenths from the larger: 6 − 2

quiz.q: Which length is the longest?
quiz.explain: 75/10 = 7 5/10. Compare wholes: 8 1/10 and 8 have 8; 8 1/10 has 1 tenth more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 9 tenths beats 1 tenth even with a smaller whole

quiz.q: A ribbon is 2 m, 3 tenths of a metre and 5 hundredths of a metre long. Write its length as a mixed number.
quiz.explain: 3 tenths = 30 hundredths, and 30 + 5 = 35 hundredths. So 2 35/100 m.
quiz.mistake: Writes the tenths and hundredths in the wrong order

quiz.explain: 45 + 78 = 123 hundredths = 1 whole and 23 hundredths. 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry the extra whole
Subtracts 20 from 65 instead of borrowing

quiz.q: How many hundredths make 3 tenths?
quiz.explain: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 3 tenths = 30 hundredths.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a tenth and a hundredth are the same size

quiz.q: Rehan ran 1 4/10 km in the morning and 2 9/10 km in the evening. How far did he run in all?
quiz.explain: 1 + 2 = 3 wholes. 4 + 9 = 13 tenths = 1 3/10. Total 4 3/10 km.
quiz.mistake: Drops the extra whole made by 10 tenths

teach.ask: Gappu added 2 6/10 + 1 7/10 and wrote 3 13/10. Is that finished? Help Gappu tidy it up!
teach.praise: Neat and tidy! Gappu's answer is now 4 3/10.
teach.nudge: What can Gappu do with 10 of those 13 tenths?

learn.hook: Is 0.5 smaller than 0.45 because it has fewer digits? Nope! Let's find out why.
points: After the decimal point the places are tenths, hundredths, thousandths, and so on.
Each place is 10 times smaller than the place to its left.
In 3.04 the 4 is in the hundredths place, so its value is 0.04.
To compare decimals, first compare the whole parts, then tenths, then hundredths.
Zeros at the end after the point do not change the value: 0.5 = 0.50 = 0.500.

steps: Compare tenths: 4.07 has 0 tenths, 4.7 has 7 tenths

learn.reallife: When comparing the prices ₹45.50 and ₹45.05, or race times like 12.4 s and 12.35 s, you compare decimals.

games.title: Decimal detective
items: A zero at the end after the point does not change the value.
0.25 has 2 tenths and 0.3 has 3 tenths, so 0.3 is greater.
In 6.738 the digit 3 is in the hundredths place.
7 is tenths, 3 is hundredths and 8 is thousandths.
A decimal with more digits is always the bigger number.
0.123 has more digits but is smaller than 0.5.
The whole part 2 is less than 3, so 2.9 is smaller.

quiz.q: What is the place value of 6 in 25.36?
quiz.explain: 6 is the second digit after the point, which is the hundredths place. Its value is 6 hundredths = 0.06.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the first place after the point is hundredths

quiz.q: Which is greater: 0.8 or 0.75?
quiz.explain: Compare tenths: 0.8 has 8 tenths and 0.75 has 7 tenths. So 0.8 is greater. (0.8 = 0.80 and 80 > 75.)
quiz.mistake: Thinks 75 is bigger than 8, so 0.75 must be bigger

quiz.q: Which list goes from smallest to largest?
quiz.explain: Write them as hundredths: 0.29, 0.30 and 0.31. Now it is easy to see 29 < 30 < 31.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the number with fewer digits is the smallest

quiz.q: A number line from 2 to 3 is cut into 10 equal parts. A dot sits on the 4th mark after 2. What number is it?
quiz.explain: Each small part is one tenth. 4 tenths after 2 is 2.4.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each small part is a hundredth

quiz.q: Riya's long jump was 3.45 m and Kabir's was 3.5 m. How much farther did Kabir jump?
quiz.explain: Write 3.5 as 3.50. Then 3.50 − 3.45 = 0.05 m. Kabir jumped 5 cm farther.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 3.45 is longer because 45 is more than 5

quiz.q: In 47.293, which digit is in the hundredths place?
quiz.explain: After the point: 2 is tenths, 9 is hundredths and 3 is thousandths.
quiz.mistake: Counts places from the left of the whole number

quiz.q: Which number is equal to 5.3?
quiz.explain: Adding a zero at the end after the point does not change the value, so 5.3 = 5.30.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any zero changes the value, even at the end

quiz.explain: 1 one, 2 tenths, 5 hundredths and 3 thousandths make 1.253.
quiz.mistake: Puts the digits in the wrong places

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 0.35 is bigger than 0.4 because 35 is bigger than 4. Help him compare them correctly!
teach.praise: Tweet! 4 tenths beats 3 tenths — Gappu will never be fooled again!
teach.nudge: Which place after the point should we compare first?

learn.hook: A medicine tablet may hold 500 mg of medicine — that is just half a gram! Decimals help us switch between such units.
points: Read 42.573 as 'forty-two point five seven three' — say each digit after the point.
₹1 = 100 paise, so 5 paise = ₹0.05 and ₹7.35 = 7 rupees 35 paise.

example.q: A packet has 2 kg 75 g of rice. Write the weight in kg.

learn.reallife: Shop bills show ₹ with two decimal places for paise, and food labels show weights in g and kg.

quiz.q: What is the expanded form of 6.47?
quiz.explain: 6 is ones, 4 is tenths and 7 is hundredths.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the tenths and hundredths places

quiz.explain: There are no hundredths, so a 0 goes in that place: 35.208.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 0 for the missing hundredths

quiz.q: How is 12.05 read?
quiz.explain: After the point the digits are 0 and 5, so we say 'point zero five'.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the zero after the decimal point

quiz.q: Write 375 g in kg.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 100 instead of 1,000

quiz.q: A bag of sugar weighs 2.3 kg. How many grams is that?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 100 instead of 1,000

quiz.q: A tablet contains 250 mg of medicine. How many grams is that?
quiz.mistake: Divides by 100 instead of 1,000

quiz.q: What does ₹8.05 mean?
quiz.explain: The two digits after the point are paise: 05 paise = 5 paise.
quiz.mistake: Reads 0.05 as 50 paise

quiz.q: Kiran has 15 rupees and 40 paise. How is this written in rupees?
quiz.mistake: Puts 40 paise in the wrong decimal places

teach.ask: Gappu found a coin box with 3 rupees and 5 paise. Gappu wrote ₹3.5. Is that right?
teach.praise: Correct! ₹3.05 — Gappu won't lose 45 paise now.
teach.nudge: How many paise make ₹1, and so what decimal is 5 paise?

learn.hook: Your height might be 1.45 m — that tiny dot lets a single number hold metres AND centimetres!
points: 1 cm = 10 mm, so 1 mm = 0.1 cm.
1 kg = 1000 g, so 1 g = 0.001 kg. Also 1 km = 1000 m.
₹1 = 100 paise, so 50 paise = ₹0.50.
To add or subtract decimals, line up the decimal points, fill empty places with zeros, then work as usual.

example.q: Aisha buys 1 kg 250 g of rice and 750 g of dal. What is the total weight in kg?

learn.reallife: Tailors measure cloth in metres like 2.25 m, shops weigh vegetables as 1.5 kg, and bills show rupees and paise like ₹36.75.

quiz.q: A pencil is 8 cm 4 mm long. What is its length in cm?
quiz.explain: 10 mm = 1 cm, so 4 mm = 0.4 cm. The pencil is 8 + 0.4 = 8.4 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there are 100 mm in a cm

quiz.q: Write 65 cm in metres.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 10 instead of 100

quiz.q: A bag of atta weighs 2.5 kg. How many grams is that?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 100 instead of 1000

quiz.q: Kabir has ₹12.50. He spends ₹4.75 on juice. How much money is left?
quiz.explain: Line up the points: 12.50 − 4.75 = 7.75.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the smaller paise digit from the bigger one instead of borrowing

quiz.q: Meena walked 1.25 km to the market and then 0.8 km to her aunt's house. How far did she walk in all?
quiz.explain: Line up the points: 1.25 + 0.80 = 2.05 km.
quiz.mistake: Lines up the last digits instead of the decimal points (1.25 + 0.08)

quiz.q: Which is longer: 1.5 m or 145 cm?
quiz.explain: 1.5 m = 150 cm, and 150 cm is more than 145 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 145 is bigger than 1.5 without changing the units

quiz.q: Write 3 kg 40 g in kg.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 40 g is 0.4 kg

quiz.q: Riya has a 5 m ribbon. She cuts off 1.75 m for a rangoli border. How much ribbon is left?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to write 5 as 5.00 and slips while borrowing

teach.ask: Gappu wants to add 2.5 kg and 1.25 kg of mangoes. How should he add decimals?
teach.praise: Hooray! 3.75 kg of mangoes — Gappu is ready for a mango party!
teach.nudge: What must be in line when we write the numbers one below the other?

learn.hook: Zoom in on a number line like a camera, and between 2.7 and 2.8 you'll find 2.71, 2.72, 2.73 ...!
points: To place 2.7, cut the gap from 2 to 3 into 10 equal parts and count 7 parts after 2.
To place 2.74, zoom into the gap 2.7 to 2.8, cut it into 10 parts and count 4.
To read a mark, first find the size of one small step: (end − start) ÷ number of parts.
To find which decimal is closest to a target, work out each distance from the target and pick the smallest.
learn.reallife: A thermometer between 37 °C and 38 °C has 10 small marks — a nurse reads 37.4 °C from the line.

items.text: From 3 to 4 cut into 10 parts, the 6th mark is ___
From 0.4 to 0.5 cut into 10 parts, the 3rd mark is ___

games.title: Line logic
items: When 0 to 1 is cut into 100 equal parts, each part is 0.01
On a line from 0 to 2 with 20 equal parts, each part is 0.1

quiz.q: The gap from 7 to 8 is cut into 10 equal parts. What number is at the 3rd mark after 7?
quiz.explain: Each part is 0.1, so 3 parts after 7 is 7.3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each part is 0.01

quiz.q: A line from 0 to 1 has 10 equal parts. A dot is 2 marks before 1. What number is it?
quiz.explain: Each part is 0.1. Two parts back from 1 is 1 − 0.2 = 0.8.
quiz.mistake: Counts from 0 instead of back from 1

quiz.q: Zoom in: the gap from 4.6 to 4.7 is cut into 10 equal parts. What is at the 5th mark after 4.6?
quiz.explain: Each part is 0.01, so 5 parts after 4.6 is 4.65.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each part is still 0.1

quiz.q: A line from 2 to 4 is cut into 20 equal parts. How big is each part?
quiz.mistake: Assumes every line has 10 parts per unit without checking

quiz.q: On the line from 2 to 4 with 20 equal parts, a dot is at the 13th mark after 2. What number is it?
quiz.explain: Each part is 0.1, so 13 parts = 1.3. 2 + 1.3 = 3.3.
quiz.mistake: Writes the mark number after the decimal point

quiz.q: Which number is closest to 5?
quiz.mistake: Thinks numbers below 5 are always closer

quiz.q: Which number is closest to 0.5?
quiz.explain: Distances from 0.5: 0.02, 0.05, 0.095 and 0.1. 0.48 is closest.
quiz.mistake: Compares digits instead of distances

quiz.q: What number is exactly halfway between 3.4 and 3.5?
quiz.explain: Zoom in: 3.40 to 3.50 has 10 hundredth-steps; halfway is 5 steps: 3.45.
quiz.mistake: Adds the tenths digits 4 + 5 to get 3.9

teach.ask: Gappu must put 2.74 on a number line but only sees marks for 2 and 3. How can Gappu do it?
teach.nudge: Which two tenths does 2.74 lie between?

topics.title: Adding and subtracting decimals with care

learn.hook: 7 − 3.46 looks tricky. Write 7 as 7.00 and it becomes an ordinary borrowing sum!
points: Pad with zeros so both numbers have the same decimal places: 5.6 − 2.37 → 5.60 − 2.37.
Regroup like whole numbers: 10 hundredths = 1 tenth and 10 tenths = 1 one.
Borrow across places when needed: 4.00 − 1.68 = 2.32.
Estimate from whole parts: 12.7 + 8.45 is between 12 + 8 = 20 and 13 + 9 = 22.
In a decimal sequence, find the step and continue: 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, ... adds 0.25 each time.
learn.reallife: Counting change at a shop — ₹50 minus a bill of ₹37.85 — uses the same padding and borrowing.

games.title: Line them up
items: Adding a zero at the end does not change 5.6.
Each term is 0.2 more than the one before.

quiz.mistake: Does not pad with a zero and subtracts digits in the wrong places

quiz.explain: 7.00 − 3.46: borrow across the places to get 3.54.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that borrowing reduces the ones digit

quiz.explain: Hundredths: 5 + 8 = 13 → write 3, carry 1. Tenths: 7 + 6 + 1 = 14 → write 4, carry 1. Ones: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry from the tenths to the ones
Subtracts only the whole parts and the hundredths

quiz.q: Without adding exactly, between which two numbers must 23.6 + 14.8 lie?
quiz.explain: Whole parts: 23 + 14 = 37. Each number is less than 1 more, so the sum is less than 24 + 15 = 39. (Exactly 38.4.)
quiz.mistake: Uses only one of the two bounds

quiz.q: What comes next: 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, ...?
quiz.mistake: Thinks the step is 0.1

quiz.q: What comes next: 5.4, 5.1, 4.8, ...?
quiz.explain: Each term is 0.3 less, so 4.8 − 0.3 = 4.5.
quiz.mistake: Adds the step instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Which shows the correct way to line up 12.5 + 3.75?
quiz.explain: Line up the decimal points and pad 12.5 to 12.50 so both have two decimal places.
quiz.mistake: Lines up the last digits instead of the decimal points

teach.ask: Gappu wrote 3.5 + 1.25 = 1.60 by adding 35 + 125. What should Gappu do instead?
teach.nudge: What must Gappu line up before adding?

learn.hook: 2.5 hours is NOT 2 hours 50 minutes! Some dots only look like decimal points.
points: Hours have 60 minutes, so 2.5 hours = 2 hours 30 minutes. 1 foot = 12 inches, so 5.5 feet = 5 feet 6 inches.
Decimal slips can be dangerous: 0.5 ml and 5 ml of medicine differ by 10 times.
To compare a fraction with a decimal, write both the same way: 3/5 = 0.6, which is more than 0.58.
In digit puzzles, put the biggest digits in the biggest places to get close to a large target.
learn.reallife: Cricket scores show overs like 12.4 — that means 12 overs and 4 balls, because an over has 6 balls, not 10!

games.title: Real or look-alike?
items: Half a foot is 6 inches, since 1 foot = 12 inches.
A dose of 0.5 ml is the same as 5 ml

quiz.q: How many minutes are there in 1.5 hours?
quiz.explain: 1.5 hours = 1 hour + half an hour = 60 + 30 = 90 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Treats an hour as 100 minutes

quiz.q: Raj is 4.5 feet tall. (1 foot = 12 inches.) Which is the same height?
quiz.explain: 0.5 foot = half of 12 inches = 6 inches.
quiz.mistake: Reads the digit after the point as inches

quiz.q: A doctor prescribes 2.5 ml of syrup. By mistake 25 ml is measured. How many times the correct dose is that?
quiz.explain: 25 ÷ 2.5 = 10. A small slip with the decimal point makes the dose 10 times too big.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts instead of finding how many times

quiz.q: Write 3/4 as a decimal.
quiz.mistake: Writes the numerator and denominator as digits

quiz.q: Write 1/5 as a decimal.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1/5 is 0.5 because of the 5

quiz.q: Which is greater: 3/5 or 0.58?
quiz.mistake: Thinks the decimal with more digits is bigger

quiz.q: Which is the smallest?
quiz.mistake: Does not convert the fractions before comparing

quiz.q: Using the digits 2, 5 and 7 once each in ☐.☐ + 0.☐, which sum is closest to 8?
quiz.explain: Put the biggest digit, 7, in the ones place: 7.5 + 0.2 = 7.7. The others give 5.9, 3.2 and 5.9.
quiz.mistake: Puts a smaller digit in the ones place

teach.ask: Gappu says the movie is 2.5 hours, so it is 2 hours 50 minutes. Is Gappu right?
teach.praise: Correct! Gappu will reach the cinema on time now.
teach.nudge: How many minutes are in one hour, and what is half of that?
